stories.title: User Signs In
stories.prompt: What happens when a user signs in?
stories.goal: to access the application with their account
stories.benefit: their identity, session, and access level are established before they continue
conversation: Sign-in starts from an existing users row; account creation and password reset are outside this story.
The schema stores the active login in sessions and derives access context from user_roles and roles.
permissions is an action catalog without declared role links in this sample, so it is useful context but not part of the authenticated relation path.

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing account with valid credentials
acceptance_criteria.when: the user submits the sign-in form
acceptance_criteria.then: the matching users row is found by email and its password_hash can be verified
a sessions row is created for that users.id with an expires_at timestamp

acceptance_criteria.given: the signed-in user has assigned roles
acceptance_criteria.when: the app loads the authenticated context
acceptance_criteria.then: user_roles links the user to roles that describe their access level

playback.text: The sign-in attempt begins by finding the existing account in users, using email as the login identifier and password_hash for credential verification.
playback.spoken_text: Sign-in starts by finding the existing account and checking the submitted credentials against the stored login details.

playback.text: After the account is verified, the new session is attached to users.id so later requests can resolve the session token back to the signed-in account.
playback.spoken_text: Once the account is verified, the app creates a session so future requests can be traced back to this signed-in user.

playback.text: Authorization context fans out through user_roles, which uses the same users.id identity anchor to find each role assignment.
playback.spoken_text: Then the app looks up the user's role assignments, building the access context from the same identity.

playback.text: Each role assignment resolves to roles, giving the app named access levels for the authenticated user.
playback.spoken_text: Each assignment resolves into a named role, giving the app a clear access level for this session.

playback.text: With the session token active and roles loaded, the app can treat the request as signed in and apply permission checks from the available access catalog.
playback.spoken_text: With the session active and roles loaded, the app can handle the request as authenticated and apply the right permission checks.

stories.title: Customer Places Order
stories.prompt: Make another story for big sample.
stories.goal: to place an order and complete payment
stories.benefit: the business can fulfill the purchase and collect revenue against a clear invoice
conversation: This story follows an existing customer through checkout; customer acquisition and lead conversion are outside the flow.
The sample schema separates the operational order from the billing invoice, so the playback shows fulfillment first and billing second.
Inventory tables exist in the fulfillment cluster, but there is no declared order-to-stock reservation relationship in this schema.

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing customer with selected products
acceptance_criteria.then: orders is linked to customers by customer_id
order_lines links the order to each purchased product

acceptance_criteria.given: the order is ready for billing
acceptance_criteria.then: invoices and invoice_lines record the billable total for the order
payments records the amount and paid_at timestamp against the invoice

playback.text: The checkout flow starts from customers, the account that owns the purchase and anchors the commercial history.
playback.spoken_text: First, checkout starts with the customer account. This is the record that owns the purchase history.

playback.text: A new orders row is created for that customer, using orders.customer_id to connect the purchase to the account.
playback.spoken_text: Next, the app creates the order and attaches it to the customer, so the purchase has a clear owner.

playback.text: Each selected product becomes an order_lines row, connecting the order to products with quantities.
playback.spoken_text: Then each item in the basket becomes an order line, connecting the order to the products and quantities being bought.

playback.text: Product lookup completes the line-item context, letting fulfillment and billing calculate what was bought.
playback.spoken_text: The product reference fills in what each line item represents, which is what fulfillment and billing need next.

playback.text: Billing generates an invoices row from the order, separating the operational purchase from the amount due.
playback.spoken_text: Billing then creates an invoice from the order, turning the purchase into an amount due.

playback.text: invoice_lines breaks the invoice into billable charges, preserving the detail behind the invoice total.
playback.spoken_text: Invoice lines preserve the detail behind the bill, so the invoice total can be explained later.

playback.text: When payment is captured, payments links the paid amount back to invoices so the order can be treated as paid.
playback.spoken_text: Finally, the payment is recorded against the invoice, marking the commercial side of the order as paid.

stories.title: Customer Opens Support Ticket
stories.prompt: Make another story which also connects to other stories.
stories.goal: to get help after a purchase
stories.benefit: support can respond with the right customer and account context
conversation: This story follows the order story as a post-purchase support moment, even though tickets are linked to customers rather than directly to orders.
Support messages can be traced back to users through ticket_messages.sender_user_id, so the flow depends on an authenticated sender when the customer or agent posts a message.
Knowledge base articles and feedback are modeled separately from tickets; the playback includes them as a self-service path after the case is created.

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer needs help after checkout
acceptance_criteria.then: tickets records the subject and status against customers.id

acceptance_criteria.when: the customer or agent posts a reply
acceptance_criteria.then: ticket_messages links the message to both the ticket and the sender user

acceptance_criteria.given: the issue can be answered by documentation
acceptance_criteria.when: the customer reads a knowledge base article
acceptance_criteria.then: feedback can record whether that article was helpful

playback.text: The support flow starts from customers, carrying forward the account context established by the earlier order story.
playback.spoken_text: The support flow starts with the customer account, carrying forward the context from the purchase.

playback.text: A tickets row captures the new case and links it to customers.id, so support can see which account needs help.
playback.spoken_text: A new support ticket is created and attached to the customer, so the support team knows which account needs help.

playback.text: The first conversation entry is stored in ticket_messages and tied back to the ticket with ticket_id.
playback.spoken_text: The first message is stored under the ticket, creating the conversation thread for the case.

playback.text: ticket_messages.sender_user_id connects the reply to users, which is why this story depends on the sign-in story for authenticated authorship.
playback.spoken_text: The message also points to the signed-in user who wrote it, connecting support activity back to authenticated identity.

playback.text: If the case is answered through self-service, articles provides the knowledge base content that can resolve the issue without another ticket update.
playback.spoken_text: If the issue can be solved through self-service, a knowledge base article can provide the answer.

playback.text: feedback records whether the article helped, closing the loop from support demand back into knowledge base quality.
playback.spoken_text: Finally, article feedback records whether the answer helped, so support can improve the knowledge base over time.
